deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen observatory, 25 March 1819. The heading reads 'New examination of the division lines from 15° to 15°', circle West ('Kr. in W'). The aim is to determine the graduation (division) errors f(x) of a divided circle at the 24 lines x = 0°, 15°, …, 345°. Karl Ludwig Harding read one reading microscope on each of two full rotations: microscope II the first time, microscope III the second. The lower microscope I was set each time exactly on the true division line x. The index ('Schnabel') stood at −35′.

(1) Data. For every x Gauss records two readings: the microscope II reading (small, about ±2″) and the microscope III reading (about 25–29″). He groups them in sets of four lines 90° apart: x, x+90, x+180, x+270, for x = 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75. Following the next page, call the II readings a, b, c, d and the III readings A, B, C, D.

(2) Model (my reconstruction, consistent with all the numbers and with the next page). Take microscopes II and III to sit about 90° on either side of I. Then the II reading at line x is a = p + f(x−90) − f(x), and the III reading is A = q + f(x+90) − f(x), up to a common sign convention. It follows that b+A = c+B = d+C = a+D = p+q identically, so f drops out.
- The 6×4 block of numbers (27.20, 26.70, 29.05, 27.78 | 26.85, … | …, 27.80) is exactly these 24 sums. Example for x=0: b+A = 1.50+25.70 = 27.20, c+B = 0.60+26.10 = 26.70, d+C = −0.10+29.15 = 29.05, a+D = −0.32+28.10 = 27.78.
- All 24 sums estimate the same constant. Their mean is 'Mittel 27″18' (exactly 652.23/24 = 27.17625).

(3) Reading error. Each sum contains two readings, so Var(sum) = 2m², where m is the mean error of one reading. One constant is estimated from 24 values, leaving 23 degrees of freedom. Hence m² = S(x−μ)²/(2·23) = S/46.
- Gauss first wrote 0.327354, which equals the same S divided by 69 = 3·23. He struck it out and corrected it to S/46 = 0.491026, so S ≈ 22.587.
- This gives m = √0.491026 = 0.7007 ≈ 0″701.

(4) Division errors. The next page gives the formula used here: f(x) = u − (b+D)/3, and cyclically f(x+90) = u − (c+A)/3, f(x+180) = u − (d+B)/3, f(x+270) = u − (a+C)/3. The constant u is fixed so that the four values of each group sum to 0.
- For x=0 this gives u = 36.91/4 = 9.2275, and f(0) = −0.639, f(90) = +0.461, f(180) = +0.561, f(270) = −0.383.
- These match the tabulated −0.64, +0.46, +0.56, −0.38. All 24 tabulated values (with 360 repeating 0, and 180 written twice) come from this formula.

(5) Harmonic fit. Gauss fits the first harmonic: f(x) ≈ −0″59 cos x + 0″32 sin x, with more decimals −0.59071 and +0.31655. These are essentially the least-squares (discrete Fourier) coefficients a = (1/12)Σ f cos x, b = (1/12)Σ f sin x. The 'Calc' column is this formula evaluated at each x. The residuals 'die übrigbleibenden Differenzen' are observed minus calc for x = 0…165 (first column) and 180…345 (second column).

(6) Residual scatter. Gauss records:
- 'Summe der Quadrate' 0.5549;
- 'Mittl. Werth' 0.5549/24 = 0.02312 (dividing by 24, not 22);
- square root 0″152.

(7) 'Stand der Mikroskope gegen I' (positions of the microscopes relative to I):
- II: +0.12, which is the mean of the 24 II readings (2.78/24 = 0.116);
- III: +27.06 = 27.18 − 0.12, the mean of the III readings (649.45/24).
This uses the fact that Σf = 0, so the mean of each microscope's readings is its constant.

(8) Hindsight from the next page. Gauss there declares the formula of step (4) wrong and replaces it by u − [3(b+D) − (d+B)]/8. Under the model, b+D = 2f(x) − f(x+90) − f(x+270) + const, which equals 3f(x) + f(x+180) + const once the group sum is zero. The formula used on this page dropped the f(x+180) term. Solving the pair for x and x+180 gives the corrected expression [3(b+D) − (d+B)]/8, as Gauss later wrote. Consequently every f on this page is f_w(x) = f(x) + f(x+180)/3, so the odd (first-harmonic) part is underestimated by the factor 2/3 (my inference).
errors: The basic formula f(x) = u − (b+D)/3 neglects the contribution of f(x+180). Gauss himself states on the next page that it is wrong and should be u − [3(b+D) − (d+B)]/8. Hence the tabulated f values and the harmonic coefficients (−0.59, +0.32) are biased: the first-harmonic amplitude is too small by a factor 2/3. The true fit would be about −0.89 cos x + 0.47 sin x.

Recomputing S(x−μ)² for the 24 sums from the transcribed readings gives about 23.09, not 22.587. That would give m² ≈ 0.502 and m ≈ 0″709 instead of 0″701. Either one reading is transcribed or read differently, or there is a small arithmetic slip.
The first divisor 69 (giving 0.327354) was wrong. Gauss corrected it on the page to 46 = 2·23.
Residual at x=285: −0.40 − (−0.46) = +0.06, but +0.08 is written.
Residual at x=300: −0.65 − (−0.57) = −0.08, but the entry (partly blotted) appears as −0.30.

Sum of squares of residuals: with the written entries (+0.08, −0.30) the sum is 0.6549, not 0.5549, so there is apparently an addition slip of exactly 0.1. With the correct residuals (+0.06, −0.08) it is about 0.568, giving mean 0.0237 and root 0″154. The final 0″152 is therefore almost unaffected.
The residual mean square is divided by 24 rather than 24−2 = 22, which is inconsistent with the n−1 logic used for m above. This is minor.

The fitted coefficients do not exactly reproduce a direct discrete Fourier computation from the rounded tabulated f values: that gives a ≈ −0.586 and b ≈ +0.333 versus Gauss's −0.5907 and +0.3166. Gauss probably used unrounded values or a slightly different procedure; the differences are small.

results.what: Determination of circle division errors by rotating the circle under three reading microscopes about 90° apart. Sums of readings from two microscopes are formed so that the division errors cancel, giving a check constant (27″18) and an internal estimate of the reading error.
results.modern_name: Calibration of graduated circles by the method of rotating reading microscopes (closure / self-calibration of angular scales)
results.usually_credited_to: Developed by Bessel (Königsberg, from 1819 onward), Hansteen and others in the early 19th century

results.what: Mean error of a single reading as √(S(x−μ)²/(2(n−1))), using n−1 because the mean is estimated, and a factor 2 because each datum is a sum of two readings. Gauss first divided by 3(n−1), then corrected to 2(n−1).
results.modern_name: Unbiased variance estimator with degrees-of-freedom correction (n−1)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria combinationis observationum, 1821/1823); Bessel used related formulas around 1815–1818

results.what: Least-squares fit of the periodic division error by a first harmonic, f(x) ≈ a cos x + b sin x, with residuals and their mean square.
results.modern_name: Harmonic (Fourier) analysis of periodic graduation error by least squares
results.usually_credited_to: Bessel's treatment of division errors by periodic series (1820s); harmonic least squares generally to Gauss/Bessel

results.what: Zero-sum normalization of the division errors over each 90° cycle, and microscope positions taken as the means of their readings.
results.modern_name: Gauge fixing / closure condition in angular self-calibration

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observatory reduction work: division-error calibration of a new meridian circle with Harding. The mild points of interest are the explicit n−1 (2·23 = 46) correction in March 1819, before Gauss's published 1821/23 treatment, and a first-harmonic least-squares fit of the division errors. The page also uses a flawed formula that Gauss himself corrects on the next page. Nothing here would change historical attributions.

checkable.asserts: Mean of the 24 sums b+A etc. is 27.17625 ≈ 27''18
The struck value 0.327354 is the same S divided by 69 instead of 46 (difference ≈ 0)
Sum of squared deviations ≈ 23.09 (Gauss's implied value is 22.587)
Formula u-(b+D)/3 etc. with zero group sum reproduces f(0)=-0.64, f(90)=+0.46, f(180)=+0.56, f(270)=-0.38
Least-squares first-harmonic coefficients ≈ -0.586 and +0.333, close to Gauss's -0.5907, +0.3166

checkable.sympy: f1,f2,f3,f4,k=symbols('f1 f2 f3 f4 k'); bD=2*f1-f2-f4+k; dB=2*f3-f4-f2+k; simplify((3*bD-dB-2*k).subs(f4,-f1-f2-f3)/8 - f1)
checkable.asserts: Under the model with zero group sum, [3(b+D)-(d+B)]/8 recovers f(x) exactly (result 0), confirming Gauss's correction on the next page
Mean of microscope II readings ≈ 0.116 ≈ +0.12 (Stand II); 27.18-0.12 = 27.06 (Stand III)

transcription_corrections: The value at x=0 for microscope II reads −0,32 but appears overwritten (possibly over −0,12). The value −0,32 is consistent with the sum a+D = 27.78.
In the 'Mittlerer Ablesungsfehler' line, the denominator 46 is written over an earlier figure, and 0,327354 is struck through and replaced by 0,491026.
Stand der Mikroskope gegen I: III should read +27,06. This agrees with 27.18 − 0.12 and with the mean of the III readings.

Residual list, second column, 9th entry (x=300): the sign is blotted and it reads ~0,30, though the computed value is −0,08. The 6th entry (x=255) has its last digit overwritten ('+0,05'). Several minus signs in the 'Calc' column (315, 345) and the residuals are heavy blots, not separate symbols.
Formula line: the coefficients are −0,59071 (for cos x) and +0,31655 (for sin x). The transcription's '+31655' is missing '0,'.
'H. P. Harding' = Herr Professor Harding (Karl Ludwig Harding). 'Kr. in W' = Kreis in West.
